definition: Typography arranges type through choices such as typeface, size, spacing, and line length to support reading and convey hierarchy or character.
example: A designer increases line spacing and distinguishes heading weights to make a long article easier to scan.

definition: Ubersuggest is an SEO research application for exploring search keywords, ranking estimates, competitors, and site issues.
example: A content strategist compares estimated demand for several candidate search phrases before planning an article.

definition: UglifyJS is a JavaScript parser, compressor, and mangler used to shrink source files while preserving intended behavior.
example: A build process produces a smaller script by removing unnecessary whitespace and shortening local variable names.

definition: UI patterns are reusable solutions to recurring interaction and interface design problems.
example: A designer uses progressive disclosure to keep optional invoice controls out of the default form.

definition: UIkit is a front-end web framework that supplies CSS and JavaScript components for building interfaces.
example: A developer combines UIkit grid and navigation components to lay out a responsive page.

definition: UIKit is Apple's framework for constructing interfaces and handling user interaction and application events on supported platforms such as iOS and iPadOS.
example: An iOS developer uses a view controller to present a list and handle selection.
sense_note: Distinct from the UIkit front-end web framework.

definition: UiPath is an automation platform for designing, running, and managing software workflows, including robotic process automation.
example: A team builds an approved workflow that copies validated invoice data between existing business applications.

definition: UltraTax CS is tax preparation software used by tax professionals to prepare and electronically file supported returns.
example: A preparer imports client information and reviews diagnostics before submitting an authorized return.

definition: Ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy measures how a sample absorbs or transmits ultraviolet and visible light as a function of wavelength.
example: An analyst compares a sample's absorbance against calibration standards to estimate concentration.

definition: Unbounce is a web platform for creating and testing landing pages used in marketing campaigns.
example: A campaign team compares conversion rates for two approved versions of a registration page.

definition: Underscore.js is a JavaScript utility library with functions for working with collections, objects, functions, and templates.
example: A developer uses its grouping function to organize records by a shared category.

definition: Unified endpoint management administers computers, mobile devices, and other endpoints through a common platform for configuration, policies, updates, and inventory.
example: An IT team checks laptop and phone compliance with organization policy from a shared console.

definition: Unisys MAPPER is a legacy data management and application development environment for interactive reporting and business applications.
example: A modernization team maps a historical MAPPER report to the equivalent fields in a replacement application.
sense_note: Historical product naming may vary; verify the installation.

definition: Unity is a game engine and editor for building and deploying interactive two-dimensional and three-dimensional applications.
example: A developer attaches a C# script and collider to a character object and tests its movement in a scene.

definition: Unreal Editor is the graphical authoring environment for Unreal Engine, used to construct levels, set up assets, and configure gameplay.
example: A level designer places lights and collision geometry and previews a playable route in the editor.

definition: Usability testing observes people attempting representative tasks to identify where an interface or service helps or hinders their work.
example: A researcher watches participants attempt to update a delivery address and notes where they hesitate or fail.

definition: UsabilityHub was the name of a remote design research platform, later branded Lyssna, for collecting feedback through tasks such as first-click and preference tests.
example: A designer compares where participants initially click on two proposed navigation layouts.

definition: A use case diagram represents external actors and the goal-oriented interactions they have with a system, without detailing the steps inside each interaction.
example: A diagram shows that customers can request refunds while only managers can approve certain requests.

definition: User Datagram Protocol is a connectionless transport protocol that sends discrete datagrams without guaranteeing delivery, ordering, or duplicate suppression.
example: A voice application uses UDP for audio frames because it can tolerate occasional missing frames.

definition: User experience design shapes how a person understands, uses, and feels about a product or service across interactions and contexts.
example: A team redesigns an appointment journey from finding availability through changing a booking after confirmation.

definition: User interface design defines the presentation and behavior of the controls, content, and feedback through which a person interacts with a system.
example: A designer specifies the labels, focus states, and error messages for a payment form.

definition: User provisioning software creates, updates, and deactivates accounts and assigned access in response to authorized identity lifecycle changes.
example: An organization removes departing workers' access to connected applications when their accounts are deactivated.

definition: User research systematically studies people's needs, behaviors, contexts, and experiences to inform design and product decisions.
example: Researchers interview appointment schedulers and observe their work before proposing changes to the booking workflow.

definition: UX writing creates the words in a product or service interface that help people understand options, complete tasks, and recover from errors.
example: A writer changes a vague error into a message that explains which field needs correction and preserves entered information.

definition: A validation protocol is a documented plan that specifies how evidence will be gathered to show that a system, process, or method meets requirements for its intended use.
example: A manufacturing team defines test cases and acceptance limits before assessing a new inspection system.
sense_note: Broad quality or compliance sense; the domain and governing standard are unspecified.

definition: Data validation checks whether data conforms to rules for type, format, range, consistency, or other intended-use requirements.
example: An import rejects a record with an invalid date and reports which field failed the check.

definition: Valuation of options estimates the value of contingent rights to transact under specified terms by modeling factors such as underlying price, volatility, time, and exercise rules.
example: An analyst compares model prices of otherwise similar options with different expiration dates.
sense_note: Financial derivative sense; other contexts can refer to real options or comparing alternatives.

definition: A value proposition states the benefit an offering promises to a defined audience and why it is worth choosing over alternatives.
example: A scheduling tool's proposition explains how clinic staff can reduce missed calls without adding another shift.

definition: Value stream analysis examines the end-to-end flow of work and information needed to deliver a result to identify delay, waste, or opportunities for improvement.
example: A clinic maps the steps from referral to appointment and finds that requests sit in an unreviewed queue between teams.

definition: A variable-frequency drive controls the speed or torque of a compatible AC motor by varying the frequency and voltage of its electrical supply.
example: A facility varies pump speed to match demand rather than running the pump at a single speed.

definition: Variance analysis compares actual results with planned or standard values and investigates reasons for material differences.
example: An accountant separates a materials cost overrun into differences attributable to purchase prices and quantities used.
sense_note: Interpreted as managerial accounting; distinguish from statistical analysis of variance.

definition: Varnish Cache is a reverse proxy that caches eligible HTTP responses and serves them without contacting the origin on every request.
example: A publisher uses it to serve cached copies of public article pages during a surge.

definition: The VAX 4000 is a family of Digital Equipment Corporation computer systems based on the VAX instruction set architecture.
example: A systems historian identifies peripherals compatible with an archived VAX 4000 configuration.
sense_note: Historical product family; configurations vary by model.

definition: The VAX 8000 is a series of higher-end Digital Equipment Corporation systems implementing the VAX instruction set architecture.
example: A computer archivist identifies a VAX 8800 system from its model documentation.
sense_note: Historical product series; not a single configuration.

definition: VAXELN was a Digital Equipment Corporation environment for developing and running real-time applications on supported processors, notably VAX systems.
example: A preservation team reviews VAXELN task documentation to understand a legacy industrial controller.
sense_note: Historical environment; verify exact version and target hardware.

definition: Vector search retrieves items by comparing numerical vector representations using a distance or similarity measure, often with an approximate nearest-neighbor index.
example: A document search system retrieves paragraphs whose embeddings are close to the embedding of a question.

definition: VectorWise is a former name associated with the Actian Vector analytical database, a column-oriented system using vectorized query execution.
example: An analyst runs aggregations over selected columns in a large fact table.
sense_note: Historical product naming; distinguish vectorized SQL execution from embedding similarity search.

definition: Veeva provides cloud software for life sciences operations such as clinical, regulatory, quality, and commercial workflows.
example: A regulatory team manages approved document versions in a Veeva Vault application.
sense_note: Vendor and product-family label; exact Veeva application is not specified.

definition: Vehicle inspection examines a vehicle against specified safety, condition, emissions, or other criteria and records findings.
example: An inspector documents tread condition and verifies that required exterior lights work.

definition: Vehicle maintenance preserves safe and reliable operation through scheduled service and correction of identified faults.
example: A fleet technician replaces worn brake components and records the repair for future service planning.
